  • Seeking guidance, Murdock returns to Clinton Church and sits with Father Lantom. Murdock shares that he desires to kill Fisk, but that meeting Marianna has made his desire waiver, which Lantom tells him is a sign, urging Murdock that the darkness of such an act will only spread.[156][145]
  • Cardenas is murdered by Junkie Jake.[156][145]

4th

  • Matt Murdock arrives at the office, where he is met by Foggy Nelson and Karen Page. Page shares the names of the two men who attacked her outside of Elena Cardenas' Apartment as Stewart Schmidt, and Joseph Pike, Westmeyer-Holt Contracting employees, but that both of them have turned up missing. The trio excitedly unwrap a newly made Nelson and Murdock plaque for the outside of the door, but Page receives a call, informing her that Elena Cardenas has been murdered.[156][145]
  • At the 15th Precinct Police Station, the trio identify the body as Cardenas'. Brett Mahoney fills them in on the details of her murder. As Nelson and Page comfort each other, Murdock quietly struggles to contain his anger.[156][145]
  • The trio go to Josie's Bar to drink and remember Cardenas. On the tv, Wilson Fisk gives his condolences for Cardenas, feigning sympathy, further worsening the trio's already dour mood. Murdock decides to leave.[156][145]
  • Murdock suits up to search for the killer.[156][145]
  • The Man in the Mask eventually finds Junkie Jake and interrogates him on why he murdered Cardenas. Jake, afraid of the man, tells him that he was paid for the job at a warehouse on Pier 81. When Murdock leaves.[156][145]
  • Murdock arrives at Pier 81, but learns it was a trap set up by Nobu Yoshioka. Yoshioka informs the man that he is here to kill him, after their previous encounter.[156][145]
  • At Josie's, a now drunk Page tries to comfort Nelson as he cries, upset with how the city continues to fail people.[156][145]
  • Duel at Pier 81:
    • Yoshioka throws shuriken at Murdock, who deflects them with his batons. Murdock and Yoshioka furiously attack each other, until Yoshioka unveils his kyoketsu-shoge, and begins swinging it as Murdock runs towards him. Murdock is able to evade several attacks, but is sliced multiple times by Yoshioka's blade. The blade strikes a hanging light, creating sparks before knocking Murdock into a barrel of flammable liquid. Yoshioka admits that his is honored to be the one to kill the Masked Man, before slicing him several more times along his back and torso. Yoshioka drags a bleeding Murdock across the ground, but Murdock is able to rise, and kicks Yoshioka into the liquid. Yoshioka counterattacks and his blade hits another light, creating sparks that ignite the liquid, engulfing him in flames.[156][145]
    • Fisk and Wesley arrive, hoping that the two had killed each other, but upon seeing the masked man alive, Fisk admits to the murder of Cardenas. An enraged Murdock attacks Fisk, but his is unable to overpower him in his weakened state, so Fisk leaves him on the ground to be killed by Wesley. However, Murdock is able to escape by jumping out a window.[156][145]
  • A nearly dead Murdock manages to get back to his apartment. Nelson arrives, wanting to visit his friend, and hearing the commotion, rushes inside, discovering the half-dead Masked Man. Upon removing his mask, Nelson is horrified to discover that his identity is that of Matt Murdock.[156][145]
  • Nelson tries to get Murdock to the hospital, but he calls Claire Temple upon Murdock's insistence.[104][145]

5th

  • Junkie Jake is pushed off a building by Wilson Fisk's men.[104][145]
  • Matt Murdock wakes up and assess his injuries, shocked to find Foggy Nelson in the apartment. An upset Nelson demands answers from his lifelong friend.[104][145]
  • Murdock explains his powers, and Nelson flips him off, asking if he can tell how many fingers he is holding up, which Murdock confirms as just one. Nelson asked if the Bombing of Hell's Kitchen was his fault, but Murdock says that it was Wilson Fisk, further upsetting Nelson, who wants his friend to be safe. Karen Page calls, and Nelson begrudgingly covers for Murdock, saying he was hurt in a car accident.[104][145]
  • Madame Gao and Fisk meet on a rooftop and discuss Nobu Yoshioka's death and Gao's worry that she is next and that Fisk is losing his way.[104][145]
  • At Metro-General Hospital, Ben Urich visits his wife, Doris and the pair share a tender moment together before her memory fails and she forgets the conversation, upsetting Ben. Shirley Benson gives Ben the unfortunate news that she could not get him the extension.[104][145]
  • Nelson looks at Murdock's vigilante suit, questioning how he knows how to fight. Murdock tells his friend about Stick. Murdock explains how he can sense people's emotions and intentions, which Nelson is disgusted by.[104][145]
  • In his office at the New York Bulletin Building, Urich researches hospice care centers for his wife, but is interrupted by Mitchell Ellison wanting to check in on him. Ellison offers him an editor job to help him out, and Urich says he will think about it.[104][145]
  • Page arrives at office and is surprised to find Urich there. He urges her to be careful and gives him all the evidence he has on Fisk, wanting to retire and lay low for a while due to his wife's condition. Page, tricks Urich into continuing the case by offering to take him to a care center upstate, and Urich agrees to go.[104][145]
  • As they prepare for a fundraiser at the Van Lunt Building, Fisk asks Leland Owlsley to reassure Gao. After Owlsley questions Fisk he stresses that change is inevitable, and Vanessa Marianna is here to stay.[104][145]
  • As Murdock gets dressed, Brett Mahoney calls Nelson and informs him of Junkie Jake's death, noting Nelson's anger, Murdock stresses that the law is not always enough, and that this is why he puts on the mask.[104][145]
  • Page and Urich arrive at Saint Bénézet Retirement Care, and upon Page's insistence, Urich looks around despite the price.[104][145]
  • Nelson presses his friend, asking for more reasoning. Murdock shares that over the years he tried to ignore the sounds of people who needed help, but that eventually, it came to be too much, and he attacked a man who abused his daughter. Nelson sees though this, believing it is just an excuse to hurt people.[104][145]
  • Urich and Page encounter Marlene Vistain, who they discover is Fisk's mother. Urich realizes this was all part of Page's plan, upsetting him, but he plays along with Page and asks Vistain to tell them about her son.[104][145]
  • Attack on Vanessa Marianna: Fisk gives a speech at the fundraiser, vowing to help those in need as a result of the Masked Man's "attacks." Fisk mingles with the party goers, but the festivities end when several guests fall ill, including Marianna, horrifying Fisk.[104][145]
  • Murdock questions if Nelson would have put on the mask if it meant saving Elena Cardenas, angering Nelson. Nelson yells at his friend, who begins crying, that he puts him and Page in danger, as they would be considered accessories to any crimes Murdock does. Crying, Murdock manages to say that the city needs him, but Nelson states that he only needs his friend, before leaving the apartment.[104][145]
  • Nelson goes to the office and throws away the name plate, ending he and Murdock's partnership.[104][145]
  • Fisk rushes Marianna to Metro-General Hospital, scared for her life. The doctors take her into the ER, leaving Fisk in the waiting room.[157][145]

6th

  • Jonathan Pangborn is admitted to hospital for recovery. He is given treatment three times a week for the next few weeks.[158]
  • The demolition process begins on Elena Cardenas' Apartment building.[157][145]
  • Karen Page visits Matt Murdock, who is recovering in his apartment. She questions him on the details of his accident, but he lies to her and refuses to give straight answers. Page informs Murdock on her findings with Marlene Vistain, and Wilson Fisk killing his father. Page gifts Murdock a balloon before leaving.[157][145]
  • Foggy Nelson wakes up at Marci Stahl's Apartment, upset about the events of yesterday. Stahl tires to console him, but is unsuccessful.[157][145]
  • At Metro-General Hospital, James Wesley voices his believe that Vanessa Marianna may have been poisoned by Madame Gao to Leland Owlsley, who suggests that he thinks it may have been the Japanese. Wesley asks Owlsley to watch the finances of both, and to speak with Gao.[157][145]
  • Claire Temple visits Murdock and stiches the wounds he opened, she urges him to take it slower, suggesting he get some armor of some kind. Murdock remembers the armored suit Fisk was wearing when they fought. Temple leaves, telling Murdock she is leaving the city for a while, and Murdock tanks her for everything she has done for him.[157][145]
  • Page and Ben Urich meet at the docks. Urich voices how much Page's actions the night prior upset him. Page agrees that she should have told him her plan, but insists it was necessary in order for Urich to learn about Fisk's past. Urich tells Page about the Attack on Vanessa Marianna, leading Page to belive it was meant to be a attack on Fisk, to which Urich agrees.[157][145]
  • Wesley comforts a stressed out Fisk, informing him on who he and Owlsley suspect. Fisk tells Wesley to make arrangements to send Marianna away once she has recovered, to protect her.[157][145]
  • Murdock goes to Clinton Church, finding Paul Lantom there. Lantom questions Murdock's reason for being here, asking if it was the same reason as last time. Murdock admits he did not kill Fisk, and is conflicted on if he should have. Murdock recounts how he believes his powers were part of God's plan for him, that he exists only to stop the bad people of the city, and Lantom agrees its a possibility, but that Murdock should use his calling to thread the path of the righteous.[157][145]
  • Back at his apartment, Murdock meditates, remembering his battle with Nobu Yoshioka.[157][145]
  • Murdock, as the Masked Man hunts down Turk Barrett and chases him across the rooftops. Upon catching up to him, Berrett agrees to talk without the need for fighting, so Murdock asks him for the person who made Fisk's body armor. Berrett gives up the name Melvin Potter.[157][145]
  • Fisk gets a call from his mother, but ignores it so he can tend to Marianna. Outside the room, Fisk asks Wesley to return his mother's call and see what she needs. Fisk returns to the room and asks to be left alone. Owlsley returns and recounts his conversion with Gao, saying that she did not poison Marianna, before heading home. Wesley calls Fisk's mother, who tells him about her encounter with Ben Urich and Karen Page the night before.[157][145]
  • Infiltration into Melvin Potter's Workshop: The Masked Man sneaks into Melvin Potter's Workshop, finding the armored suit material. Potter returns to his shop as Murdock approches him. He questions Potter, but he throws a punch at Murdock, leading to a brief scuffle.[157][145]
  • Wesley asks Francis for his gun, asking him to protect Fisk, before leaving to find Page.[157][145]
  • Potter and Murdock continue fighting, until Murdock is able to put Potter in a chokehold and he yields. Potter begins crying, telling the man that Fisk will hurt Betsy Beatty if he gives up any info. Murdock vows to protect the both of them if Potter helps him with making a protective suit.[157][145]
  • Page finds Foggy Nelson drinking at Josie's Bar. She decides to join him, berating him for not communicating with her. A discouraged Nelson says that the story about Fisk's father will not hold any water before asking about Murdock. Page asks what happened between them, but he refuses to give any specifics.[157][145]
  • as Urich researches Bill Fisk, Page calls him, to see if he is doing okay and reveal that everything with Nelson and Murdock is falling apart. Urich tells her that she just needs to do what she can, and she thanks him for the advice.[157][145]
  • Page is kidnapped by Wesley before she gets to her apartment.[157][145]
  • Fisk promises to the sleeping Marianna that the people who did this to her will suffer, and that not even God could stop him.[157][145]
  • Kidnapping of Karen Page: Page wakes up in a warehouse, across from Wesley. Wesley reminds her that she signed the NDA, and was supposed to go away, as it was decided she was not a threat and did not not to be killed. Wesley sets a gun on the table to intimidate her, mentioning her visit with Marlene Vistain. Wesley warns her that Fisk would be very upset to learn about what she had done, but he offers her the chance to live, by using her skills to work for Fisk. Page scoffs at the idea, but Wesley tries to convince her, by waring that he would kill everyone whe cared about, but he is interrupted by a call from Fisk, allowing Page the chance to grab his gun, and shoot him until the clip was empty. Panicked, Page takes the gun and runs .[157][145]
  • Page throws the gun into the river and returns to her apartment.[159][145]
  • Overwhelmed, Page drinks to num the pain. She then quickly takes a shower, before falling asleep[159][145]

7th

  • In the early hours, Karen Page wakes up from a nightmare of Wilson Fisk killing her in revenge.[159][145]
  • Page heads to the Nelson and Murdock Law Office, trying to get her mind off of what happened, but is unable to. Foggy Nelson arrives and startles her, apologizing for how the last few days have been. Nelson promises that in spite of he and Matt Murdock's falling out, he will continue the Wilson Fisk case. Page questions him on his opinion regarding the Masked Man, with Nelson replying that he no longer thinks he is a terrorist, before asking Page to call him if she needs anything.[159][145]
  • Murdock arrives at the office, also apologizing for his recent behavior. Page admits that she feels like she made a mistake working here, but that he and Nelson are the only good things in her life. Murdock questions if something happened to her, and she says yes, not giving any specifics.[159][145]
  • Fisk waits by Vanessa Marianna's bedside as she wakes up, asking what happened. Fisk tells her that she was poisoned at the fundraiser, apologizing for putting her in danger, informing her that she will be protected by Fisk's men overseas for a while. Marianna wishes to stay, wanting nothing to separate the pair. Fisk is informed by Francis that James Wesley has been murdered.[159][145]
  • Fisk, Leland Owlsley, and his men find Wesley's body. Francis informs Fisk that Wesley asked for a gun and a car before heading out on his own, leading to his death, angering Fisk. Fisk sits next to the body of his closest friend, tearfully saying goodbye after dismissing everyone from the room. Fisk checks Wesley's phone and notes that Marlene Vistain was the last person he called.[159][145]
  • The Masked Man approaches Ben Urich, asking for information on Steel Serpent. Urich informs the man that Madame Gao is responsible for its distribution now in the Russian Mafia's absence. Thankful for the help, the man tells Urich to watch his back, as Fisk is an animal.[159][145]
  • Nelson meets with Marci Stahl at Josie's Bar, with a request for help. When he mentions Fisk, she tires to leave, as Landman and Zack is representing him, but Nelson urges her to stay, so she agrees.[159][145]
  • Page goes to Ben Urich's Apartment to inform him that she believes Fisk knows about their visit to his mother. Inside, the pair work on finding a second source for the information Vistain gave them. Page attempts to stress the importance of posting the story now, and Urich says he will see what he can do.[159][145]
  • Nelson shares all his information on the Fisk case, and asks Stahl to trust him, and help bring him down and earn her soul back, worried about her career, she is hesitant, but agrees to help.[159][145]

8th

  • Matt Murdock heads into the city, using Ben Urich's information about Steel Serpent. He locates one of Madame Gao's drug runners and follows them.[159][145]
  • Murdock scales the rooftops and follows the car until it arrives at Madame Gao's Warehouse. From the rooftop, he watches the runner go inside.[159][145]
  • Mitchell Ellison's son has a cello performance at school, and Ellison attends.[159][145]
  • Urich arrives at the New York Bulletin Building, looking for Ellison.[159][145]
  • Wilson Fisk picks up his mother, and explains to her that Saint Bénézet Retirement Care is no longer safe, and that he is taker her to live in Italy. He asks his mother is she remembers James Wesley, and why he called her the other night. She struggles to recall.[159][145]
  • Karen Page calls Urich, asking if he has been able to speak with Ellison, he confirms that he hasn't. Murdock calls Page and tells her he will need the day off, and that he is working on something that will help.[159][145]
  • Ellison returns to work and Urich hands him the Fisk story. Ellison is very displeased with the story, knowing there is no source and it will only lead to a lawsuit. Urich keeps pushing him to print it, so Ellison suspends him for the week, however, Urich continues, and Ellison retorts that Fisk is spending millions to save the city. Urich questions what Fisk is paying Ellison, which sets him off, so Ellison fires Urich, claiming his stories lately have been shit.[159][145]
  • Infiltration into Madame Gao's Warehouse: In Gao's warehouse, the guards hear a noise and investigate it, but are defeated by the Masked Man. The man sees all the blind workers, but is interrupted by Gao commanding them all to run towards Murdock.[159][145]
  • Leland Owlsley and Fisk discus leads on Wesley's killer. Owlsley suggests the Man in the mask, but Fisk denies this as a possibility, as he does not kill. Fisk gets a call, which forces him away from the conversation.[159][145]
  • The remaining guards begin firing at Murdock, but he manages to incapacitate them, however, the stay bullets hit a barrel of gas, starting a fire. Murdock questions the worker's blindness, but Gao tells her they had faith in something bigger than themsleves, and that he had taken that away. Murdock leaves to save the workers, helping them all to escape the burning building. As the NYPD arrive, Murdock tries to escape, but Brett Mahoney puts him under arrest. Murdock pins Mahoney down, and tells him that he did not kill officer Christian Blake, and that he along with other officers are in Fisk's pocket, before letting Mahoney go and running off.[159][145]
  • Gao meets with Owlsley, telling him about the Masked Man's infiltration into her heroin production. The pair discus their attempted murder of Vanessa Marianna. Owlsley questions if she had killed Welsey, and she admits he would never, as Wesley had never wronged her. She then says her goodbyes before returning to her homeland.[159][145]
  • Urich goes to Metro-General Hospital to visit his wife, he offers to take her to Paris, like they had always talked about. She recognizes that he has a story he wants to tell, but he admits that he was fired. Doris encourages him to write the story on the internet, since he never needed the New York Bulletin.[159][145]
  • Ben Urich calls Page, explaining to her his plan to write a blog exposing Fisk since he was fired from the Bulletin. She wishes him a goodnight before he heads home. Murdock returns to the office, telling Page she should go home. Page questions if the three of them will ever go back to normal. Murdock recalls Stick's teachings, saying that you have to push away the people you love in order to succeed, but that he knows that he can't do this alone. He starts breaking down, but is hugged by Page, who says he is not alone.[159][145]
  • Murder of Ben Urich: Urich returns to his apartment and begins writing about the Fisk story. However, he soon notices that Fisk had broken into his apartment. Urich demands he leave, but Fisk requests a simple honest conversation. Fisk apologizes for thinking that Urich's days of being relevant were behind him, but that he tries to learn from his mistakes. Before he leaves, he asks if Urich was alone when he met with Vistain, to which Urich replies that he was alone, so Fisk then admits that because of that he is here to kill him. Fisk lunges at Urich and chokes him out, murdering him.[159][145]

9th

  • Jonathan Pangborn has x-rays taken of his serious injuries and the operations performed.[158]

10th

  • Cassietta George's cover of Silent Night is released.[3][160]

11th

  • Pym Technologies posts on Google+ saying: "Pym Technologies has been supporting ideas for improved sensory-technology. Swarm robots with no sensory limitations? We think yes. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant_robotics)."[161]

13th

  • Ben Urich's funeral is held, with Matt Murdock, Karen Page, Mitchell Ellison, Paul Lantom, M. Caldwell, Silvio, Ben's wife Doris, and her nurse Norma all attending. Everyone looks on as Urich's coffin was lowered into his grave.[162][145]
  • After the service, Page speaks with Doris, who tells Page about his admiration of her. Page tries to apologize for getting Ben involved with the story, but Doris corrects her, saying Ben never does a story he did not want to do. The pair share a tearful moment mourning Ben before Doris leaves.[162][145]
  • Lantom asks how Murdock is holding up, and he states that he blames himself. Lantom tells him that he shouldn't, before everyone heads home.[162][145]
  • Page and Murdock arrive at the office, and Page questions Foggy Nelson's absence from the funeral. Page admits that every time she closes her eyes she worries that Wilson Fisk will find out that she was with Urich at Saint Bénézet Retirement Care. Murdock promises to protect her, and that Fisk will get what it coming to him soon.[162][145]
  • At his penthouse, Fisk and Vanessa Marianna discuss the plan to keep her overseas, with Fisk noting an irregularity in his finances.[162][145]
  • Murder of Leland Owlsley: Fisk meets with Leland Owlsley, who remarks that they need to find a replacement for Madame Gao, now that she has disappeared. Fisk asks Owlsley to look at some irregularities in his finances, knowing Owlsley was responsible. Fisk pins James Wesley's death on him, but he denies any involvement, however, Fisk deduces that the Attack on Vanessa Marianna was done by Owlsley. Owlsley attempts to blackmail Fisk to save himself, stating that Carl Hoffman, who has been working with him, will rat on Fisk if Owlsley doesn't check in every hour, but Fisk ignores this and lashes out, pushing Owlsley down an abandoned elevator shaft, killing him.[162][145]
  • Nelson approches Murdock as he trains at Fogwell's Gym. Nelson mentions that he figured Murdock would be out wearing the mask, and Murdock states that he was, attempting to see if Ellison was working for Fisk, but was unable to find out for certain. Murdock berates Nelson for missing the funeral, but Nelson says that he was going to go, but was interrupted by Marci Stahl sending him some documents from Landman and Zack relating to Fisk. Murodck warns him that Stahl is now in danger, but vows to stop Fisk now. Nelson reminds him of what happened last time. Murdock questions how he can stop Fisk, and Nelson reminds him that the law is what they do, adding that he wishes to find a way to move forward. Murdock agrees.[162][145]

14th

  • A fire occurs in the church of Santa Maria de las Flores in Miami, Florida. The entire church burns down, except for a painting which is over 500 years old. This painting has the Words of Creation etched into its back. The priest of the church decides to organize an event so as to raise funds and rebuild the church.[163][90][164]
  • After the completion of Operation Cerberus, William Rawlins returns to the United States to continue his work as Deputy Director of Covert Affairs.[63][165]
  • Matt Murdock and Foggy Nelson meet with Brett Mahoney at the 15th Precinct Police Station to get information of Ben Urich's killer. Mahoney is unsure, but tells the men about his run in with the Masked Man, and that he said the NYPD is in Wilson Fisk's pocket. Officer Corbin walks by, and Murdock overhears him mention that he is searching for Carl Hoffman, who is in hiding. Mahoney heads back inside, and Murdock tells Nelson that they need to find Hoffman.[162][145]
  • At the office, Murdock, Nelson, and Karen Page work together on reading through Marci Stahl's Landman and Zack paperwork in order to find information on where Leland Owlsley is keeping Hoffman, knowing if Hoffman talks, they could bring down Fisk's operation. Page finds a discrepancy in Silver & Brent's property holdings, meaning that must be Hoffman's location, so Murdock heads there.[162][145]
  • Fisk answers a phone call from one of his men, informing him that Hoffman had been found, so he orders them to execute him.[162][145]
  • Rescue of Carl Hoffman: Inside an abandoned, church, Owlsley's men are attacked by Fisk's officers, leaving Hoffman as the sole survivor. As Hoffman accepts his fate, the Masked Man arrives and subdues the officers, saving him. The man sits with Hoffman, and explains the opportunity at hand. He offers Hoffman's guaranteed safety in return for testifying against Fisk, Hoffman agrees once the man suggests that Nelson and Murdock would defend him.[162][145]
  • Hoffman reaches the 15th Precinct and tells Mahoney that he needs to make a statement.[162][145]
  • Nelson, Murdock, and Page represent Hoffman, and ask that he be put in protective custody in exchange for the information he will provide. Hoffman spills all the information he knows, including senator Randolph Cherryh's involvement with Fisk's criminal enterprise.[162][145]

15th

  • The Home Reference to Holistic Health and Healing: Easy-to-Use Natural Remedies, Herbs, Flower Essences, Essential Oils, Supplements, and Therapeutic Practices for Health, Happiness, and Well-Being is released.[3][166]
  • Using Carl Hoffman's information, the FBI arrest many of Wilson Fisk's associates.[162][145]
  • The FBI capture Turk Barrett as he runs away.[162][145]
  • The FBI find Officer Corbin, who is arrested and escorted away from the 15th Precinct Police Station.[162][145]
  • The FBI arrest New York Bulletin employee M. Caldwell, upsetting Mitchell Ellison, who realizes that Ben Urich was right all along.[162][145]
  • Landman and Zack partner Parish Landman is detained by the FBI for his involvement, as Marci Stahl looks on, feeling proud.[162][145]
  • Senator Randolph Cherryh is detained due to accepting bribes from Fisk.[162][145]
  • As they watch his empire fall apart, Fisk orders for Vanessa Marianna to be moved to Europe.[162][145]
  • Arrest of Wilson Fisk: The FBI storm into Wilson Fisk's Penthouse and arrest him, as he gives Marianna a ring as a final gift. He expresses his love for her as he is dragged away. Downstairs, Fisk is placed into the FBI convoy as he ignores the press' questions.[162][145]
  • At the office, Nelson, Murdock, and Page celebrate the news of Fisk's arrest, proud of what they have all done. They toast to Elena Cardenas, Ben Urich, and everyone else Fisk has hurt.[162][145]
  • In the police van, Fisk recounts the Parable of the Good Samaritan, stating that he is no longer the good Samaritan, but rather the ill intent. As the convoy reaches a bridge, they are ambushed by dozens of Fisk's corrupt NYPD officers, leading to a shootout in the street. Fisk remains calm as his officers decimate the FBI.[162][145]
  • Nelson, Murdock, and Page watch the news in horror as Fisk's convoy is attack, before suggesting they head home before the streets are closed down. They send Page home in a cab, despite her insistence on them coming with her. Nelson asks Murdock to stay safe, and not die while stopping Fisk before heading home.[162][145]
  • The officers reach Fisk's van and free him. Fisk is then escorted into an unmarked truck, and transported to a secure location.[162][145]
  • Murdock meets with Melvin Potter, who introduced him to the new armored suit he requested. Murdock thanks him for the suit, and promises he will protect Betsy Beatty, as promised.[162][145]
  • Donning the suit, Murdock listens for Fisk's location, and begins to track him down. He overhears Fisk as he arrives at a garage and is moved into a different truck. Fisk instructs Marianna to leave if he has not joined her in twenty minutes' time, but he assures her that they will be reunited eventually.[162][145]
  • Duel of Hell's Kitchen:
    • Murdock ambushes the truck, causing it to flip over. As Fisk exits, he is face to face with the man in the mask, Daredevil. Daredevil uses his billy clubs to fend off Fisk's remaining guards, as Fisk runs away.[162][145]
    • Daredevil peruses Fisk into an alleyway, cornering him. Fisk berates Daredevil, as he took everything from him, vowing to kill him. The two men charge into battle, and Fisk throws Daredevil onto the ground, but he retaliates with a series of punches and kicks. Fisk grabs Daredevil and slams him into the wall, eventually throwing him down again. Fisk grabs a pipe and swings it at Daredevil, striking his helmet. Daredevil uses his billy clubs to counter Fisk, but is caught off guard, grabbed by Fisk, and pinned to the ground. Fisk grabs the billy club and angrily beats Daredevil with it, screaming that the city doesn't deserve his better tomorrow, however, Daredevil is able to regain control of his club, using it to beat Fisk until he is knocked down.[162][145]
    • Mahoney arrives, and realizes that Daredevil is the masked man, and he just stopped Fisk. He reports finding and detaining Fisk, and allows Daredevil to go.[162][145]
  • Marianna is saddened when Fisk misses the window, so she dons the ring before departing, longing to see him again.[162][145]

16th

  • The New York Bulletin publishes a paper on last night's brawl, titled "Daredevil Collars Fisk."[162][145]
  • Foggy Nelson, Matt Murdock, and Karen Page gather outside their office to hang the Nelson and Murdock plaque back up and celebrate Wilson Fisk's arrest. Page notes the masked man being called "Daredevil" in the paper, and the three agree on liking the name. Nelson says goodbye to his friends, as he needs to help Marci Stahl find a new job. Page and Murdock reflect on the events that led them here, and remark that they are glad to have done it together.[162][145]
  • Fisk is escorted by NYPD officers to Rikers Island. Upon arrival, he is ordered to remove his suit and cufflinks.[167][145]
  • Fisk sits in his cell at Rikers Island and stares at the wall, noting its similarity to Rabbit in a Snowstorm.[162][167][145]
  • That night, Murdock dons the Daredevil suit and heads out for another night of crimefighting.[162][145]

17th

  • Wilson Fisk's attorney, Benjamin Donovan, visits Fisk in prison, and warns him that the case was not looking good for him due to the long list of crimes he was being held accountable for.[167][168]
  • Fisk is visited by another inmate named Dutton. Dutton tells Fisk that although he may have made a name for himself on the outside, on the inside Dutton is the kingpin of the prison.[167][168]
  • Fisk is visited by Stewart Finney, who claims that he wished to meet Fisk as he felt they could help each other. Finney explains to him that Dutton controls about 80% of the contraband running through the prison. Finney presents Fisk with his allies, the violent Valdez brothers, who have a sick mother.[167][168]

18th

  • Darren Cross posts on Google+ saying "Extremely excited about virtual reality. Perhaps Pym Tech can take VR a step further? (Link - http://mashable.com/2014/12/18/street-view-virtual-reality/)".[149]

19th

  • "Youth Suffer" by Clayton Hibbert is released.[3][169]
  • So as to ensure their support, Wilson Fisk orders Benjamin Donovan to assist with Stewart Finney's case and pay the rent on the Valdez brothers' mother's home in Spanish Harlem. Fisk orders him to ensure that the transactions were untraceable.[167][168]

22nd

  • Thor and Jane Foster walk down the sidewalk. Foster leaves as Thor sees a baby in the window, reflecting on his future.[24][25]
  • WHiH World News posts late at night on Google+ saying "S.H.I.E.L.D. heavily connected to government conspiracies? More at 10."[170]

23rd

  • Government conspiracies and S.H.I.E.L.D. are discussed on WHiH World News.[170]

28th

  • Jonathan Pangborn leaves Metro-General Hospital in order to find a new way to heal his injuries. He spends the next five months trying many different spiritual treatments.[158]

29th

  • Kevin Kennedy goes into a coma.[171][172]

31st

  • Darren Cross posts on Google+ saying "The near-future of tech will change the world. And Pym Tech will be a part of that change. Happy New Year! http://mashable.com/2014/12/22/tech-trends-2015".[149][173]

  9. ↑ 9.00 9.01 9.02 9.03 9.04 9.05 9.06 9.07 9.08 9.09 In Step in the Arena, Carl Lucas/Luke Cage's hair growth would suggest approximately 4 months between his first day and nearly attacking Comanche in the courtyard, and a further 2 months between then and Squabbles being killed and Lucas/Cage being attacked again, with his escape the next day. This all takes place before January 20, 2014, the firm date for when Reva Connors is killed (see other references). Ideally, it would be a good few months at least before her death. However, in Can't Front on Me, Shades says, "My last year in Seagate, me and Comanche got paid by this juiced-in-guard, Rackham, to beat the shit out of some guy named Carl Lucas." In Code of the Streets, in November 2015 (see 2015 references), Shades says, "I just got home [...] Three years this time, Seagate," suggesting he was released in late 2015, so his "last year in Seagate" would start in late 2014, but Cage is already out and Connors is already dead by then. If Shades is taken to be very loosely meaning "just" when he says "just got home", you could maybe take it that he got home a little earlier in 2015, but still, this does not work, with Cage escaping absolutely no later than January 2014. At a stretch, it can be taken that Shades is referring to the calendar year of 2014 as his last year at Seagate, released in the first half of 2015, so only a few months in and with 2015 not counting as his last "year" - and he is also only meaning "just" loosely, back for about half a year. With this, it would mean that his second attack on Lucas/Cage, the attack that he is referring to, can be in January 2014 and still loosely fit his statement. However, with Connors killed on January 20, 2014, this is very late for Lucas/Cage's escape. At an absolute minimum, they spend a few weeks together after the escape and before her death. So, all things considered, the attack can be dated to January 1, 2014, just about fitting Shades' statement at a stretch, and allowing Cage and Connors 18 days (2nd-20th), as much as possible, living freely together before her death. This makes Lucas/Cage nearly attacking Comanche roughly November 1, 2013, and his first day at Seagate roughly July 1, 2013, based on hair growth. The rest of the flashbacks in Step in the Arena are placed between July 2013 and January 2014 accordingly.

  20. ↑ 20.0 20.1 20.2 20.3 20.4 20.5 20.6 The Bridge, The Magical Place, and Seeds all take place some time between the events of Repairs on November 23, 2013 (see 2013 references) and the events of T.R.A.C.K.S. on February 5, 2014 (see other references), with The Magical Place taking place in the days following The Bridge. The implied passage of time between episodes does not appear to be very long, with each episode appearing to be decently soon after the last. Evenly distributing these few episodes between Repairs and T.R.A.C.K.S. ends up placing the events of The Bridge and The Magical Place from December 15-19, 2013 and the events of Seeds from January 9-11, 2014. These dates end up working out quite nicely, as The Bridge and The Magical Place avoid occurring on Christmas, which would be strange for characters not to address if that were the case, and in Seeds, during her lecture with Leo Fitz at S.H.I.E.L.D. Academy, Jemma Simmons states, "We tend to forget that these organizations... Hydra, Centipede, A.I.M.... were also made up of extremely brilliant scientists, men and women who started with the same unlimited potential as you or I." The implication from this is that A.I.M., being included in the same sentence as Hydra and Centipede, is openly known to corrupt and compromised, a fact that was exposed during the events of Iron Man 3, meaning Seeds would have to occur after December 25, 2013 (see 2013 references). During said episode, Phil Coulson tells Skye that the Massacre in Hunan, which occurred around Spring 1989 (see 1980s references), happened "24 years ago," potentially suggesting the episode occurs in 2013. However, this is impossible, as it has to occur after Christmas 2013 and it cannot be during the final few days of the year due to the term being in session at S.H.I.E.L.D. Academy, forcing the episode into 2014. Seeds being a few weeks after Iron Man 3 in early to mid-January 2014 also allows enough time between the film and the episode for the aftermath of the film to settle and knowledge regarding A.I.M. to spread, as well as enough time into the term for a test to be given out as mentioned by Seth Dormer and Callie Hannigan early in the episode. Therefore, it must be taken that Coulson is either rounding down from 24.75 years for whatever reason, or is using Skye's thought-to-be age (24).

A "few" generally refers to a range of about three to five; with the amount of time between the mid-season episodes needing to be spread out as much as possible (see other references), it can be taken that Triplett and Garrett have spent five weeks tracking Deathlok, placing T.A.H.I.T.I. around early February 2014. During the pre-credits scene of T.A.H.I.T.I, on the day Yes Men begins, Jimmy Mackenzie says that he and his wife were married "yesterday." A vast majority of weddings tend to occur on Saturdays, so it can be taken that Yes Men occurs from Sunday, February 9-Tuesday, February 11, 2014, in turn placing T.R.A.C.K.S around February 5, 2014 and the majority of T.A.H.I.T.I. around February 5-6, 2014. This works nicely, as in T.A.H.I.T.I., Simmons says she has only known Skye for "a few months," with it being just under five months since the two first met on September 10, 2013 (see 2013 references), and in Who You Really Are, firmly set in Spring 2015 (see 2015 references), Coulson refers to the events of Yes Men as being "last year," dating the episode to early 2014 as opposed to late 2013.

  42. ↑ 42.000 42.001 42.002 42.003 42.004 42.005 42.006 42.007 42.008 42.009 42.010 42.011 42.012 42.013 42.014 42.015 42.016 42.017 42.018 42.019 42.020 42.021 42.022 42.023 42.024 42.025 42.026 42.027 42.028 42.029 42.030 42.031 42.032 42.033 42.034 42.035 42.036 42.037 42.038 42.039 42.040 42.041 42.042 42.043 42.044 42.045 42.046 42.047 42.048 42.049 42.050 42.051 42.052 42.053 42.054 42.055 42.056 42.057 42.058 42.059 42.060 42.061 42.062 42.063 42.064 42.065 42.066 42.067 42.068 42.069 42.070 42.071 42.072 42.073 42.074 42.075 42.076 42.077 42.078 42.079 42.080 42.081 42.082 42.083 42.084 42.085 42.086 42.087 42.088 42.089 42.090 42.091 42.092 42.093 42.094 42.095 42.096 42.097 42.098 42.099 42.100 42.101 42.102 42.103 42.104 42.105 42.106 42.107 42.108 42.109 42.110 42.111 42.112 42.113 42.114 42.115 42.116 42.117 42.118 42.119 42.120 42.121 42.122 42.123 42.124 42.125 42.126 42.127 42.128 Despite Glenn Talbot saying in Shadows, set sometime around mid-2014 (see other references), that Coulson and his team managed to evade him and the military for "an entire winter," suggesting that Captain America: The Winter Soldier and the latter half of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Season One take place around late 2013, the majority of the evidence would suggest that they take place around early Spring 2014.
    In Who You Really Are, firmly set in Spring 2015 (see 2015 references), Coulson refers to the events of Yes Men, set before The Winter Soldier, as being "last year." In Captain America: Civil War, in June 2016 (see 2016 references), Sam Wilson tells Steve Rogers that their search for Bucky Barnes following The Winter Soldier lasted "two years." At the end of The Winter Soldier, it can just barely be seen that Nick Fury's fake gravestone dates his year of death to "2014." In Inside Voices, set in May 2018 (see 2018 references), a flashback to events shortly following the climax of Beginning of the End is shown to be "four years ago." Finally, in Hot Potato Soup, in April 2017 (see 2017 references), Daisy Johnson tells Billy Koenig that the two of them have known each other for "three years," after having met at the very end of Beginning of the End. Therefore, this must mean that The Winter Soldier and the subsequent episodes of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Season One take place in 2014, discrediting a small "2013.10.12" date that can be seen in the film. Taking into consideration Talbot's line from Shadows, this would initially suggest that the film and the final half of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Season One takes place in January 2014, which would allow for most, but not all, of Winter 2013-2014 to occur after the events of the film. However, Marvel Studios' The Marvel Cinematic Universe: An Official Timeline places the events of The Winter Soldier firmly in "Spring 2014." Additionally, in End of the Beginning, a March 2014 calendar appears in the background during Deathlok's fight with Felix Blake. Finally, Skye's S.H.I.E.L.D. badge, which she is given in End of the Beginning, has an issue date of "2014MAR15." All of this, together, would suggest that the main events of The Winter Soldier span March 15-22, 2014 and End of the Beginning through Beginning of the End spans March 15-25, 2014. This fits better with the nice weather depicted in the film, which wouldn't work with January 2014, and also fits nicely with Rogers, born July 4, 1918, saying in the film that he is "95," placing the film sometime between July 4, 2013 and July 3, 2014, as well as Scarlett Johansson saying that the film is set "in real time," with March 15-22, 2014 being decently close to its real-world April 4, 2014 release date. With a firm March 2014 placement established, Talbot's line must either be discounted, or it must be taken that Talbot is conflating a period of early spring snowfall that may have occurred following the events of Season One (which is not entirely impossible, considering the Providence base's location in Ontario, Canada) as being a part of "winter," and is referring to winter coming to a resolute, "entire" close. Additionally, in the Black Widow Prelude, security footage of the climax of The Winter Soldier is dated to "17:27-04/04/14." However, considering the climax of the film occurs during sunrise/morning and not during the evening, it can be taken that this is instead when the footage was obtained or retrieved, allowing March 2014 to still work.

  58. ↑ 58.0 58.1 Through Runaways it is said that PRIDE sacrificed someone to Jonah once a year for 15 years (Fifteen: "One a year for 15 years", Hostile: "You ever notice that every year one of your young parishioners goes missing?", "Same time of year, every year", Last Rites: "One a year"), resulting in fifteen sacrifices (Fifteen: fifteen names are listed, Kingdom: "Fifteen kids have died in this room", Doomsday: "How could you murder fifteen kids?", Last Rites: "Like you killed fifteen runaways"). Fifteen annual sacrifices would amount in fact to 14 years start to finish if counting inclusively, and with the last one in October 2017 (see 2017 references), that would make the first sacrifice around 2003. However, other evidence suggests 15 years of sacrifices, so starting in 2002, rather than 14 years of sacrifices. In Fifteen, it is said they have taken runaways for "over 15 years". In Doomsday it is said that PRIDE has had a grip on the parents' "lives for the last 15 years". As well as this, Season 3 suggests there was in fact a further sacrifice (Smoke and Mirrors: "I only sacrificed seventeen innocent kids" (including Andre Compton, which the previous counts did not), Rite of Thunder: "She helped murder seventeen teenagers", Enter The Dreamland: "We are the seventeen"). Plus "one a year for 15 years" could be taken as "one a year, and we've been doing that for 15 years" rather than "one a year fifteen times, amounting to 15 years". So, it would seem overall that yes, the sacrifices started around 15 years before 2017, not 14. This, then, would make the first sacrifice 2002. This is supported by flashbacks in Metamorphosis and Doomsday, both shortly before and shortly after the first sacrifice, respectively, to "fifteen years ago" before October 2017, so sometime in 2002.
    Based on the "Same time of year, every year" line in Hostile, the first sacrifice would ideally be in October 2002. However, there is evidence suggesting earlier in 2002. Molly Hernandez was born on the firm date of November 12, 2002 (see other references), meaning she was conceived around February 2002. During the first sacrifice, Alice Hernandez does not appear visibly pregnant whatsoever, meaning this should be no later than around May 2002. Additionally, during the Doomsday flashback, set shortly after the first sacrifice, Nico Minoru appears no more than roughly a year old. With it being generally implied throughout the show that she is roughly the same age as the rest of the older Runaways, this means she should ideally be born no later than around early 2001, which would make this flashback around early 2002 at the latest. For every subsequent sacrifice, the Runaways taken in by PRIDE stayed for six months, with their six months beginning in April and the sacrifices being held annually in October. However, it's implied in Metamorphosis that Jonah gave the mansion to the Wilders not long before the first sacrifice, which would mean that either the month in which the Runaways were taken in or the month of the sacrifice was different for the first year. Considering the evidence favoring the sacrifice occurring earlier in 2002, it can be taken to be the latter, with the Runaways being taken in by PRIDE in April 2002 and Brooks Watten's sacrifice happening later that month.
    Fifteen names, up to and including Gonzalez, are shown in Fifteen, meaning there is a bonus sacrifice not listed on the computer somewhere between Brooks Watten and Destiny Gonzalez, making them between the second and fifteenth sacrifice, so it may be guessed that they were the eighth/ninth. To decide which, taking halfway between April 2002 and October 2017, it would have been roughly early 2010, making it closer to the eighth sacrifice than the ninth. So, it may have been taken to have been the eighth.
    Therefore, overall, the sacrifices were: Brooks Watten April 2002, Adam Cooper October 2003, Jamie Baxter October 2004, Tim Bennett October 2005, Xavier Marquez October 2006, Karly Scolari October 2007, James Braswyck October 2008, unknown runaway October 2009, Anthony Rocha October 2010, Kim Hwang October 2011, Bridget Bynum October 2012, John Donahue October 2013, Emily Wong October 2014, Yvonne Taylor October 13, 2015, Brian Geparhart October 2016, and finally Destiny Gonzalez (failed sacrifice) October 13, 2017 and Andre Compton October 16, 2017 (see 2017 references). Adam Cooper to Destiny Gonzalez would have been taken 6 months in advance.

She asks, "But that isn't where you served your last mission?", and Castle affirms, "No. I was part of a covert CIA operation. It was called Cerberus."   107. ↑ 107.0 107.1 107.2 Black Widow
  108. ↑ 108.0 108.1 108.2 In Black Widow, an opening montage shows several scenes of the Red Room training girls, including Natasha Romanoff, and operating through history, which is implied to be occurring after Natasha Romanoff and Yelena Belova were separated on September 6, 1995 (see other references) and before the beginning of the 2016 events of the movie on June 25, 2016 (see 2016 references).
    The first collection of scenes is of a braid receiving a bow, a group of girls being brainwashed by cartoons, and a group of girls ice skating. In the ice skating scene, the girls appear to be roughly middle school age, and can be taken to be approximately 12.5 years old. This scene can therefore be approximated to when Romanoff was 12.5 years old, so approximately June 3, 1997. The scenes with the braid and the cartoons can therefore be distributed between Romanoff and Belova being separated and the ice skating scene, so on April 7, 1996 and November 8, 1996, respectively.
    The montage also features two shots of girls marching, one of which is when they are roughly middle school age and can be taken to be approximately 13 years old, so on December 3, 1997.
    The second shot of girls marching, two shots of girls preparing weapons, a group of soldiers in a drum line, and Dreykov watching a group of girls fire at targets occur in the movie when the girls are roughly high school age. Similarly, Black Widow Prelude features a scene of a group of high school age girls doing ballet and one of Romanoff firing at a target. These can be distributed throughout the years in which Romanoff was 14 through 18 years old, placing the comic firing scene on September 19, 1998, the second marching shot on April 1, 1999, the first shot of girls preparing weapons on November 16, 1999, the ballet scene on February 13, 2001, the drum line on September 30, 2001, and the second shot of girls preparing weapons on May 16, 2002.
    Two scenes, one from Black Widow Prelude, and several flashback scenes from Avengers: Age of Ultron, both featuring Romanoff being nervous for her graduation ceremony, can be placed near the ceremony. The ceremony itself can be taken to be when Romanoff was 21, analogous to a college graduation, so May 27, 2005. Similarly, Black Widow has two scenes in which the girls are in their early twenties: one of a group of girls doing ballet, and one of a girl doing gymnastics. These scenes can be distributed between January 1, 2003, the year Romanoff turned 20, and May 27, 2005, approximately when she would graduate. This would place the Black Widow ballet scene on May 6, 2003, the gymnastics scene on September 8, 2003, the Avengers: Age of Ultron ballet flashback on May 15, 2004, the scene of Romanoff pretending to lose on September 17, 2004, Romanoff shooting on January 20, 2005.
    The montage in Black Widow then features several members of the Black Widows being spotted throughout the world, starting with Romanoff, as well as shots of a Widow putting on a Widow's Bite and a belt, and a group of Widows lining up. These scenes can be placed between the graduation and the 2016 events in Morocco on June 18, 2016 (see 2016 references), while ensuring that Romanoff's scene is before January 3, 2008, when she defected from the Red Room and joined S.H.I.E.L.D. (see 2000s references). This would place Romanoff's scene on December 25, 2006, and the rest on July 24, 2008, February 21, 2010, September 21, 2011, and April 20, 2013. A scene in this montage which is attached to this last scene can then be placed to the last day, April 20, 2013. The scene with the Widow putting on her belt and accessory, as well as the Widows marching, can then be placed on November 18, 2014.
    Three scenes from the montage feature Dreykov influencing two political events, as well as a shot of him watching his monitors. The two scenes of him influencing political events must be before Dreykov is thought dead in January 2008, and can therefore be distributed between then and Romanoff and Belova being separated. This places the first scene on October 15, 1999 and the second on November 24, 2003.
    Two events are mentioned to have happened during this period of time in The Avengers: Romanoff killing people in São Paulo and another instance of her setting a hospital on fire. These can be distributed between Romanoff's graduation and her defection, and can therefore be placed on April 9, 2006 and February 19, 2007, respectively. The Avengers: Black Widow Strikes describes an incident involving Romanoff which is described as having occurred "long before [Romanoff] defected to S.H.I.E.L.D.." This can therefore be taken to have happened within the first half of the time between graduation and defection, so on approximately January 19, 2006.
    Black Widow Prelude features a scene of Romanoff looking over New York City after joining S.H.I.E.L.D.. This would likely occur within a month of Romanoff joining S.H.I.E.L.D., so in approximately February 2008.
    The montage goes on to feature several clips of Melina Vostokoff's experiments being conducted, beginning with someone reading the information which Alexei Shostakov had stolen, a scene of pigs being studied, and a failed surgery. Later in the movie, Belova mentions that Romanoff was not subject to Vostokoff's chemical mind control, meaning that the experiment was completed after Romanoff defected and before the events in Morocco, so on approximately March 26, 2012. The person reading the stolen information can be approximated to the day after it was received, so September 6, 1995. The remaining scenes can be distributed between then and the completion of the experiment, placing the pigs on March 13, 2001 and the failed surgery on September 18, 2006.
    Finally, a group of scenes of war and a scene of a person sewing a Black Widow logo onto a piece of cloth are shown. These can be distributed throughout Romanoff and Belova being separated and the first scene and the events in Morocco, resulting in each conflict happening on July 26, 1997, June 16, 1999, May 6, 2001, March 27, 2003, February 14, 2005, January 5, 2007, November 25, 2008, October 16, 2010, and September 5, 2012, and the sewing scene on July 27, 2014.

Marvel Studios' The Marvel Cinematic Universe: An Official Timeline more specifically dates the events of the film to “Summer 2014.” With no other significant evidence to go off of, the events of the film can be taken to revolve around its real-world August 1, 2014 release date, dating the main events to around August 1-4, 2014. During the film's epilogue, the Guardians' wounds are completely healed and the Milano has been rebuilt, so it can be taken to be around a few days later, so August 8, 2014.
    Statements from James Gunn and Kevin Feige (1, 2, 3) confirm that the events of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 occur about two months after the first film, which fits with the film showing itself to be “34 YEARS LATER” after “1980.” Marvel Studios' The Marvel Cinematic Universe: An Official Timeline also dates the film to “Fall 2014”, reaffirming this. Therefore, it can ultimately be taken that the film occurs around October 2014, two months after the events of the first film in August 2014.
    The events of both seasons of I Am Groot, with the exception of Groot's First Steps, pick up shortly after Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2. Disney+'s “MCU Complete Timeline” section, as well as Marvel's official website, place both seasons of I Am Groot before Daredevil: Season One, which begins on November 2, 2014 (see other references). In order to allow a suitable amount of time to pass between each episode of I Am Groot, it can be taken that Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 takes place close to exactly two months after the first film, around early October 2014. It's unclear whether this span of two months refers to the time since the climax of the first film, dated to August 4, 2014, or the epilogue of the first film, dated to August 8, 2014, so it can be taken that the midpoint of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 occurs exactly two months after the midpoint of the climax and epilogue of the first film, placing the midpoint of the film on October 6, 2014. The film spans around three days, dating it to around October 5-7, 2014.
    While both seasons of I Am Groot are implied to take place over a relatively short amount of time, there should be at least a few days at minimum between episodes in order to allow time for Groot to get to the new locations of each episode. Therefore, in order to maximize the amount of time between episodes while having both seasons mostly occur before the events of Daredevil: Season One, it can be taken that around five days pass between episodes, which would date Season One to around October 12-27, 2014 and Season Two to around November 1-21, 2014. This works well, as it not only gives Groot close to a week between episodes, but it also places the entirety of Season Two before the midpoint of Daredevil: Season One on November 28, 2014, fitting the chronology suggested on Disney+ and Marvel's website.

145.274 145.275 145.276 145.277 145.278 145.279 145.280 145.281 145.282 There is conflicting evidence as to whether Daredevil: Season One takes place in either late 2014 or early 2015.
    • In Into the Ring, Karen Page states, "The last two years have transformed [Union Allied]," with Matt Murdock replying, "Yeah, the world watched half of New York get destroyed," suggesting that two years have passed since the Battle of New York on May 4, 2012 (see 2012 references). Although it would still be less than three full years since the Battle of New York if this were said in early 2015, this line would strongly suggest the season occurs during the calendar year of 2014.
    • In The Man in the Box, Wilson Fisk says to Murdock, "We met once before. [...] It was at an art gallery, several months ago," referring to the events of Speak of the Devil. Additionally, statements made by Charlie Cox and Deborah Ann Woll would suggest that roughly "six months" pass between Season One and Season Two. With the main events of Season Two firmly dated to October-November 2015 (see 2015 references), this would suggest Season One occurs early in the same year.
    • Over the course of the season, the general weather and climate goes from temperate to cold, with clothing worn by characters becoming heavier as the season goes along and barren trees being shown in the final couple episodes. This would imply that the season occurs closer to the end of the year when it begins to get colder (late 2014), rather than the beginning of the year when it begins to get warmer (early 2015).
    • In Reunion, in October 2017 (see 2017 references), Benjamin Donovan states, "For the past two years, ever since his unjust conviction on racketeering charges, [Fisk] has maintained his innocence and fought to clear his good name." This would seemingly imply it's been about two years since Fisk was arrested at the end of Daredevil, so around 2015, with this being the moment Fisk would've began maintaining his innocence. However, with Donovan technically only referring to the amount of time since Fisk's conviction, which happened a while after Fisk's arrest (see 2015 references), this does allow some leeway for the possibility of Fisk being arrested in 2014, with his conviction happening in 2015.
    • While speaking to Felix Manning in One Last Shot, Fisk states, "You protected her... two years. You kept Vanessa safe when I couldn't." With Fisk being arrested and thus losing the ability to protect Marianna at the end of Daredevil, this would again suggest it's been about two years since Fisk was arrested, so 2015; however, with Fisk specifically referring to the amount of time Manning himself has protected Marianna and it never being explicitly stated when exactly his protection of her began, this, as well, allows some leeway for the possibility of Fisk being arrested in 2014, with Manning perhaps beginning his protection of Marianna around early 2015.
    • On January 23, 2015, the WHiH Newsfront Google+ account posted, "Crime rate finally stable in New York. Are the Avengers to thank? Find out tonight at 10." Charlie Cox stated that the crime rate in New York City plummeted as a result of criminals being aware of Daredevil's work following the end of Season One. Based on WHiH Newsfront posting about holidays on their real-world dates and posting about Scott Lang's July 17, 2015 release from prison in the lead up to said date in real life, WHiH Newsfront can be taken to have posted in real time with their other posts as well, meaning this post referencing Daredevil was also posted on January 23, 2015 in-universe. Coupled with Cox's statement, as well as the fact that it would make very little sense for crime to stabilize in the middle of the season if it were happening in early 2015, this post would support the idea that Season One is happening in late 2014, with criminal activity across New York plummeting after Fisk's imprisonment and Daredevil becoming a known figure amongst criminals across the city in the time leading up to this post.
    • Stick abandoned Murdock when he was a child around 1995 (see 1990s references). In Stick, it's stated twice that this happened "20 years" ago, suggesting it is now around 2015, though this figure could be a result of rounding.
    • New York Bulletin newspaper props for Season One, one of which is briefly shown on-screen, contain adverts for a "Fall Special" on dental implants, suggesting that the season occurs during the fall. Additionally, throughout some of these props, there are mentions of sporting events such as the US Open, the MLB postseason, and NFL finals, all of which happen at some point during the fall, and there is a date of "Tuesday, October 14, 2014" next to a story about Jay-Z and Beyonce visiting the Louvre, which happened in real life around said date. Although not all of these events happen around the exact same time in the fall, meaning they cannot all work in conjunction with one another, they would all strongly suggest a timeframe of fall 2014.
    • In Speak of the Devil, Stewart Schmidt and Joseph Pike's IDs are shown in small dates to have been issued on "01/01/2015" and will expire on "12/31/2015", suggesting it should be after January 1, 2015.
    • In The Ones We Leave Behind, as Murdock chases after the car, barren trees with decorative lights can be seen in the background. Additionally, in Daredevil, outside the Nelson & Murdock office, a window can be seen with Christmas decorations (red and green ribbons, yellow decorative lights) and a large pine tree, potentially covered in decorative lights, can be seen down the street. During the scene, Page is holding a newspaper with a mention of an NFL "SPORTS FINAL," suggesting it's toward the end of the NFL football season, which ends around late December. All of this would heavily indicate these two episodes are happening around a December timeframe, with decorative lights and Christmas lights being put up for the holidays and the NFL season nearing its end. This would only work with late 2014.
    • In Shadows in the Glass, an article for the New York Bulletin is shown to have been published on "September 5, 2015." Though the date is incorrect whatever the case, this would maybe slightly favor early 2015 over late 2014, with at least the 2015 part being correct.
    • Murdock and Nelson left Landman and Zack shortly before acquiring their law licenses on July 20, 2014 (see other references). With the season occurring early in their legal careers, this would suggest it hasn't been very long since they left Landman and Zack, which would fit better with late 2014 as opposed to early 2015.
    • A promotional advert for Season One shows that Union Allied has plans for "Spring 2015." Though this would work just about as well with both late 2014 and early 2015, the latter would maybe work a little bit better, with the events of the show happening closer to its real world Spring 2015 release date.
    • In Daredevil, following Fisk's arrest, Nelson states, "Fisk still needs to go to trial. Just getting a court date on a case this big could take a year." Although Fisk does say in The Man in the Box that Season One was "several months ago," meaning Nelson's estimate has to have been incorrect whatever the case, this line would still suggest that the time between Daredevil and Fisk's trial/conviction, which happened no later than around mid-late 2015 (see 2015 references), is perhaps slightly longer than just a few short months if it were early 2015, thus slightly favoring late 2014.
    Ultimately, the best overall option, when weighing the evidence together and looking for any possible reconciliations or leeway that may exist, is reasoned out to be late 2014 over early 2015.
    As mentioned above, Cox and Woll both stated that approximately six months pass between seasons, with Fisk also stating in The Man in the Box that it has been "several months" since he first met Murdock in Speak of the Devil. With this in mind, it can be taken that Season One occurs as late in 2014 as is realistically possible in order to best fit these statements. While Cox and Woll's "six months" must therefore be taken as incorrect whatever the case, for Fisk's statement to somewhat work, it can be taken that he and Murdock first met in December 2014, 11 months prior to November 2015, not yet a full year. Not only does this work well with the cold weather toward the tail end of the season, but it also works well with the holidays decorations in the final two episodes. With the season spanning about a month, this would place the season as occurring from November-December 2014.
    The main events of Into the Ring begin with Murdock and Nelson acquiring their office on the same day as Page's arrest. The next day, after Murdock asks why Page has yet to be charged, Nelson states that "it's the weekend." However, Tracy Farnum tells her father earlier that day that she will swing by his apartment "this weekend," which she does at the end of the episode on the same day a weekday edition of the New York Bulletin is published. In Condemned, it's shown on a newspaper that the kidnapping of the boy at the end of Into the Ring occurred on a Friday, which fits both as being a weekday and a part of the weekend. Working backward, this means that Farnum's line can occur no earlier than the preceding Monday, which would go against Nelson's line. It can be taken that Nelson is instead referring to Page's arrest as having occurred over the weekend, on a Sunday, and that it is currently Monday. This would place the main events of Into the Ring on a Sunday-Tuesday, with a time jump of a few days to the following Friday. During the Tuesday portion of the episode, the Empire State Building can be seen to be lit red, white, and blue. In November 2014, the Empire State Building was lit this way on the night of Tuesday, November 11 for Veteran's Day, which fits nicely, so it can be taken that Into the Ring spans November 9-14, 2014.
    From here, Cut Man is said to pick up two days later, so Sunday, November 16, 2014, and Rabbit in a Snowstorm begins the following morning, so Monday, November 17, 2014. A small time jump then occurs to the start of John Healy's trial, whose cuts and bruises are still present during which, suggesting this is no more than a week later. With courthouses typically only open on weekdays and Healy's trial lasting two consecutive days, his trial ends up working best as being the following Thursday-Friday, so November 20-21, 2014. In the Blood to Condemned occurs over the following Sunday-Wednesday, based on a newspaper clipping in the latter episode saying that the shootout at Veles Taxi occurred at 3:35 AM on a Tuesday, so November 23-26, 2014.
    The main events of Stick pick up shortly afterward on a weekday, followed by Shadows in the Glass the next day, which features a small undefined gap partway through the episode. After this gap, eight consecutive days occur through to the end of The Ones We Leave Behind, which ends on a weekday based on Mitchell Ellison's son being in school that day. Taking advantage of the small gap in Shadows in the Glass, Stick can be taken to be Friday, November 28, 2014, with Shadows in the Glass beginning the next day, Saturday, November 29, 2014 before jumping to Monday, December 1, 2014, resulting in The Ones We Leave Behind finishing on Monday, December 8, 2014. This ends up placing Murdock and Fisk's meeting at the Scene Contempo Gallery on Wednesday, December 3, 2014, just about fitting the ideal December 2014 placement for this scene.
    Daredevil begins with Ben Urich's funeral, and the following day, Brett Mahoney states that the end of The Ones We Leave Behind was "a few days ago," making this no later than Sunday, December 14, 2014. The next day, many members of the New York Bulletin can be seen at work, implying it is a weekday, so it can be taken that this is now Monday, December 15, 2014. The episode concludes the next day, so December 16, 2014. This just about fits with still being in fall, with the New York Bulletin article published that day still featuring ads for the dental "Fall Special."

  168. ↑ 168.0 168.1 168.2 168.3 In Daredevil, Fisk is imprisoned on the reasoned date of Tuesday, December 16, 2014 (see other references). In Seven Minutes in Heaven, flashbacks are shown detailing his time in prison shortly thereafter. In the first scene following Fisk getting his cell, Benjamin Donovan visits Fisk. Since visitations are not allowed at Rikers Island on Tuesdays, it can be taken that this is the following day, so Wednesday, December 17, 2014, assuming this is a day where last names A-L were allowed visitors. Following this scene, Fisk is confronted by Dutton and meets Stewart Finney during a meal, both of which would've happened shortly after he arrived at the prison, so these can both be taken to be the same day as Donovan's first visit. After this, Donovan visits Fisk a second time. The earliest date this would be possible would be Friday, December 19, 2014, assuming visitations on Thursday, December 18, 2014 were reserved for inmates with last names M-Z, so this scene can be dated to said date.
